2607.02389.title: Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents
2607.02389.paper_summary: Coding agents are capable; human oversight is the bottleneck. Unconstrained agents introduce security risks, erode codebase scalability, and make human review increasingly costly. We argue that the same methods used for decades to manage large human engineering teams: access control, network policies, strict coding conventions enforced by tooling; transfer directly to coding agents, and are cheaper (in token) than recent agentic scaffolding. We sketch a start-to-end system on this principle, and report a controlled experiment in scalable oversight: a small reviewer (Gemma 4 e4b) inspects a Python codebase containing 11 inserted backdoors. Recall rises from 54.5% (unconstrained, no tools) to 90.9% (constrained substrate plus a ~200-LoC `docs` CLI), with substrate and tools contributing independently. We choose Python deliberately: substrate-level oversight gains are largest where the language gives the fewest guarantees by default; the principles extend to languages like Rust.
2607.02389.paper_summary_zh: 編碼代理是有能力的；人類的監督是瓶頸。無限制的代理會引入安全風險，侵蝕代碼庫的可擴展性，並使人類審查變得越來越昂貴。我們主張，數十年來用於管理大型人類工程團隊的相同方法：訪問控制、網絡政策、由工具強制執行的嚴格編碼慣例；可以直接轉移到編碼代理上，並且比最近的代理架構更便宜（以代幣計算）。我們在這一原則上勾勒出一個從頭到尾的系統，並報告一個可擴展監督的控制實驗：一個小型審查者（Gemma 4 e4b）檢查一個包含11個插入後門的Python代碼庫。回憶率從54.5%（無限制，無工具）上升到90.9%（有限的基底加上一個約200行代碼的`docs` CLI），基底和工具獨立貢獻。我們故意選擇Python：基底級監督的增益在語言默認提供最少保證的地方最大；這些原則擴展到像Rust這樣的語言。
2607.02389.author: Thomas Winninger et.al.
